title: Возвращение Баринова на кухню  (Barinov Returns to the Kitchen)

segments.t: Gathering the cooks in the kitchen, Lyova announces that Viktor Petrovich will be away recovering for another two weeks. As Senya jokes about the boss slacking off to drink beer, Chef Barinov himself steps out from hiding and scolds the laughing crew.
Виктора Петровича не будет еще две недели.
Он же целый месяц не работает.
Что бы я без тебя делал?
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
'May I have your attention for a minute.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'a minute' and 'attention' in a few short words.
'Anyway, here is the news.' The meaning hinges on 'short' working together with 'such' in spoken Russian. Ilya answers right away.
Виктора Петровича не будет еще две недели.
'Viktor Petrovich will be away for another two weeks.' The grammar packs 'Viktor' and 'weeks' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Он же целый месяц не работает.
'He has not worked for a whole month already.' Chef Viktor brings out the contrast between 'he' and 'already' in a few short words.
'And now he has gone off to drink beer on vacation.' Notice how Russian expresses 'now' and 'to have a drink' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Ilya answers right away.
'How can you not be ashamed of yourself?' Ilya raises the pitch on 'ashamed' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
'How could we possibly talk like that?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'how' before landing on 'to talk'.
'He is sick and he needs medical treatment.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'he' and finishing on 'is treatable'. Ilya answers right away.
'What are you all laughing at?' In Russian, the idea of 'why' flows naturally into 'to laugh loudly' without extra filler words.
Что бы я без тебя делал?
'What would I ever do without you?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'what' before landing on 'were doing'.
'Alright, alright, alright.' Notice how Russian expresses 'really?!' and 'really?!' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Ilya answers right away.
'That is enough.' Ilya anchors the line on 'come on', while 'all' completes the thought.
'So how are you doing in here?' Chef Viktor chooses the respectful plural 'you' alongside 'here' to keep a polite distance. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.

Он же целый месяц не работает.
Что бы я без тебя делал?
